'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Tammy Baldwin]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Tammy Baldwin]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) | turnout = 60.7% {{Increase}} }} {{Elections in Wisconsin sidebar}} The '''2024 United States Senate election in Wisconsin''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Wisconsin]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Senator [[Tammy Baldwin]] won re-election to a third term by a narrow 0.85% margin, defeating [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee Eric Hovde. Third-party candidates Phil Anderson and Thomas Leager were seen as potential [[Spoiler effect|spoiler candidates]] for Hovde in a state that had [[2024 United States presidential election in Wisconsin|voted for]] Republican presidential nominee [[Donald Trump]].{{Cite web |title=Democratic donors prop up far-right candidates, including a gun activist in the 2024 Wisconsin US Senate race |url=https://pbswisconsin.org/news-item/democratic-donors-prop-up-far-right-candidates-including-a-gun-activist-in-the-2024-wisconsin-us-senate-race/ |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=PBS Wisconsin |language=en-US}} This was the first time that [[Wisconsin]] voted for candidates of different political parties for U.S. senator and president since [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Gaylord Nelson]] [[1968 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|was reelected]] as [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Richard Nixon]] [[1968 United States presidential election in Wisconsin|carried the state]] in 1968. The closest of Baldwin's three Senate victories, the race held similarities to Republican [[Ron Johnson]]'s narrow win in [[2022 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|2022]], down to the percentage and raw vote margin by which the incumbents won. It was the closest Senate race in the state since [[1914 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|1914]] and the closest election ever for this seat. Baldwin won only about 4,000 votes more than [[Kamala Harris]], while Hovde received about 55,000 fewer votes than Trump. While almost all of the state's counties swung Republican compared to Baldwin's 2018 victory, Baldwin improved in [[Waukesha County, Wisconsin|Waukesha]] and [[Ozaukee County, Wisconsin|Ozaukee]]. The primary election took place on August 13, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=www.ncsl.org}} The election was considered essential for Democrats' chances to retain the Senate majority in 2024.{{cite web |title=The 10 Senate seats most likely to flip in 2024 |website=[[CNN]] |date=July 20, 2024 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/07/20/politics/senate-race-rankings-july-2024/index.html}} {{TOC limit|3}} == Background == No [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] has won this Senate seat since [[Joseph McCarthy]] in [[1952 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|1952]]. Incumbent Tammy Baldwin was first elected in [[2012 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|2012]], defeating former governor [[Tommy Thompson]] by 6 percentage points. She was re-elected in [[2018 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|2018]] by 11 percentage points.{{Cite news |title=Wisconsin |url=https://www.nytimes.com/elections/2012/results/states/wisconsin.html?mtrref=www.google.com&gwh=0A6D8CDBCDF02298B3800A5A9C15C1C2&gwt=regi&assetType=REGIWALL |access-date=2023-03-21 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}{{Cite web |title=Wisconsin {{!}} Full Senate results |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2018/results/wisconsin |access-date=2023-03-21 |website=www.cnn.com |language=en}} The race was considered to be slightly favorable to Baldwin, despite Wisconsin's nearly even partisan lean, with most polls showing Baldwin to be the favorite to win. Wisconsin is considered to be a [[Red states and blue states|purple]] state at the federal level, especially since there is both a Republican and a Democratic senator representing the state. Wisconsin was also a top battleground state in the [[2016 United States presidential election in Wisconsin|2016]] and [[2020 United States presidential election in Wisconsin|2020 presidential elections]]. The state backed the Republican candidate in 2016, and then the Democratic candidate in 2020, both by less than 1% and only a plurality.{{Citation needed|date=September 2024}} Both parties have seen success in the state in recent years. Republicans control both chambers of the Wisconsin Legislature and hold a supermajority in Wisconsin's [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] delegation. Republicans also control the state's other Senate seat. However, Democrats had seen success in statewide races, including in [[2022 Wisconsin gubernatorial election|2022]], where incumbent governor [[Tony Evers]] overperformed expectations and won reelection to a second term, despite polls showing his Republican challenger as the slight favorite.{{Cite web |title=Wisconsin 2020 presidential election results |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2020/results/state/wisconsin/president |access-date=2023-03-21 |website=www.cnn.com |language=en}}{{Cite news |title=Opinion {{!}} In Wisconsin, Tony Evers made a virtue of being dull |language=en-US |newspaper=Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2022/11/11/evers-wisconsin-governor-trump/ |access-date=2023-03-21 |issn=0190-8286}} ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== ==== Nominee ==== * [[Tammy Baldwin]], incumbent U.S. senator{{cite news |last1=Wells |first1=Dylan |title=Democratic Sen.
